_about: Expert-curated insight cards per PSI investigation, written from the PSI investigation records (data/psi_details.json) and experiment tables. 'pillars' rate relevance 0-3 to NASA's fire safety pillars. Numeric condition ranges are NOT stored here; they are computed live from data/tests.csv.

investigations.name: BASS-II
investigations.full_name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
investigations.summary: Burned real spacecraft-type solids (PMMA films/slabs/cylinders, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric) in a slow, fan-driven air flow inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox, at normal and reduced oxygen levels.
measurements: O2, CO2 and CO gas concentrations
investigations.takeaway: Shows that in microgravity a slow ventilation flow can keep solids burning at oxygen levels where they would self-extinguish on Earth, and that the NASA-STD-6001 normal-gravity screening test does not fully capture microgravity flammability.
investigations.modeling_value: Flame spread rate vs. flow speed and O2 for thin and thick fuels; extinction limits; directly usable to validate flame-spread models.
investigations.habitat_note: Highest-value solid-material data in PSI, but all tests are at or below ~22% O2. Extrapolating to 30%+ Moon-base air requires models.
investigations.earth_application: Material flammability standards, fire behaviour in enclosed and ventilated spaces (aircraft, submarines).
limitations: Flow reported as fan display, not calibrated cm/s, in the table

investigations.name: BASS
investigations.summary: First ISS campaign burning practical solid fuels (SIBAL fabric, PMMA, Ultem, etc.) in the glovebox flow duct, including wake flames and tests of an inert gaseous extinguishing agent.
investigations.takeaway: Microgravity flames over solids can survive at very low flow speeds and burn differently from the 1-g screening test; inert-gas suppression effectiveness depends on flow.
investigations.modeling_value: Flame spread and extinction over realistic geometries; baseline for BASS-II and Saffire.
investigations.habitat_note: Representative of ISS cabin air only.
investigations.earth_application: Fire behaviour behind obstructions (wake flames) in confined spaces.
limitations: O2 and pressure not varied (assumed cabin air)
Experiment table lists material and sample only

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-I
investigations.summary: First large-scale spacecraft fire: a 94 cm x 40 cm SIBAL fabric sample burned inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS.
what_varied: Flow direction: concurrent (sample S1) vs opposed (sample S2)
investigations.takeaway: Large fires behave differently from small glovebox samples: the concurrent-flow fabric fire burned for 420 s versus 70 s in opposed flow, and the vehicle-level O2, CO2 and pressure response is unique data.
investigations.modeling_value: Full-scale fire growth and cabin pressure/atmosphere response for validating vehicle-level fire models.
investigations.habitat_note: The only realistic-scale fire data; directly relevant to spacecraft and rover cabin fire scenarios.
investigations.earth_application: Large-scale fire growth in confined vehicles.

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-II
investigations.summary: Nine smaller samples of different spacecraft materials (silicone, SIBAL, PMMA, Nomex) burned in Cygnus to compare microgravity flammability with the NASA 1-g screening test.
measurements: O2 derived from measured CO2 product
Burn length and flame spread rate in microgravity and in 1-g
investigations.takeaway: Some materials that pass or fail the 1-g test behave differently in microgravity (e.g. silicone barely burned while SIBAL and PMMA sustained flames).
investigations.modeling_value: Side-by-side microgravity vs 1-g burn and spread lengths for several materials: rare paired data.
investigations.habitat_note: Material screening insight for any crewed vehicle; still only cabin-air O2.
limitations: Small number of samples per material

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-III
investigations.summary: Repeat of the large-scale fabric fire inside Cygnus at a higher flow speed (30 cm/s), in concurrent and opposed flow.
investigations.takeaway: Adds a second flow speed to the large-scale fire dataset, helping separate flow effects from scale effects.
investigations.modeling_value: Large-scale fire growth at a second flow speed.
investigations.habitat_note: Realistic-scale fire, cabin air.
investigations.earth_application: Large-scale fire growth in confined vehicles.

investigations.name: FLEX
investigations.summary: Burned isolated fuel droplets (methanol, heptane, and others) to map flammability limits and measure how well gaseous suppressants (CO2, helium) put flames out, over a range of oxygen levels and pressures.
investigations.takeaway: Quantifies the limiting oxygen index for liquid fuels with and without suppressants. CO2 is less effective in microgravity than on Earth, and FLEX also discovered long-lived 'cool flames' after visible extinction.
investigations.modeling_value: 274 individual tests with burning rate, extinction diameter and burn time; a core validation dataset for droplet combustion and suppression models.
investigations.habitat_note: Includes several tests above 30% O2 and below 1 atm, overlapping the planned Moon-base atmosphere; directly informs CO2 extinguisher sizing.
investigations.earth_application: Fire suppressant effectiveness, fuel efficiency and cool-flame chemistry for engines.
limitations: Liquid droplets, not solid cabin materials
Few tests at very low pressure

investigations.name: FLEX-2
investigations.summary: Extended FLEX to practical and two-component fuels (heptane/iso-octane, propanol/glycerol), across pressures up to 3 atm and with slow imposed flow.
investigations.takeaway: Shows how fuel mixtures and helium (a possible habitat diluent) change burning and extinction; includes up to 30% O2.
investigations.modeling_value: Benchmark bi-component droplet data; the experiment table is a condition matrix (ranges), not per-test rows.
investigations.habitat_note: Covers O2 up to 30% and sub-atmospheric pressure, the edge of Moon-base conditions.
investigations.earth_application: Cleaner and more efficient liquid-fuel combustion.
limitations: Table gives ranges only; per-test values need the raw data

investigations.name: CFI
investigations.summary: Studied low-temperature 'cool flames' of n-dodecane droplets at pressures from 0.5 to 5 atm, including helium dilution.
investigations.takeaway: Cool flames are nearly invisible, low-temperature reactions that can persist after a visible flame goes out, a hidden re-ignition hazard for fire detection and suppression.
investigations.modeling_value: Low-temperature chemistry and cool-flame extinction limits vs pressure.
investigations.habitat_note: Pressure range brackets habitat pressures; O2 does not reach 30%.

investigations.name: ACME CFI-G
investigations.full_name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.summary: Gaseous cool flames (propane, butane, ethane...) on a spherical porous burner, in normal flames and inverse flames where oxygen-enriched gas up to 85% O2 flows out of the burner.
held_constant: ACME spherical burner in the CIR
investigations.takeaway: Spans the widest oxygen range of any PSI microgravity dataset (12 to 85% O2), covering and far exceeding the 30%+ O2 expected in Moon bases and rovers.
investigations.modeling_value: 333 tests with adiabatic flame temperature, stoichiometric mixture fraction and outcome; strong validation set for high-O2 kinetics.
investigations.habitat_note: Essential for Moon-base and rover atmospheres; note inverse-flame O2 is in the oxidizer stream, not the room air.
limitations: Gaseous fuels, not solid cabin materials
Inverse-flame O2 is not ambient O2

investigations.name: ACME Flame Design
investigations.summary: Spherical ethylene and methane flames (normal and inverse) to find when flames start producing soot and when they extinguish, across oxygen, dilution and pressure.
measurements: Multispectral (HiBMs) cameras for soot temperature and volume fraction
investigations.takeaway: Maps soot-free vs sooty flames as a function of oxygen and pressure. Soot drives flame radiation and smoke, which matter for both flame spread and smoke detection.
investigations.modeling_value: 327 tests; soot inception and extinction limits with adiabatic flame temperature.
investigations.habitat_note: Covers elevated O2 and reduced pressure relevant to exploration atmospheres.
limitations: Inverse-flame O2 is in the burner stream

investigations.name: ACME BRE
investigations.summary: Used a gas-fed porous burner to emulate burning solids, testing NASA's candidate exploration atmospheres (14.7 psia/21%, 10.2 psia/26.5%, 8.2 psia/34% O2) in still air.
investigations.takeaway: Materials can burn steadily in microgravity even with ventilation off, and the explicitly tested exploration atmospheres show how flammability rises with O2. Turning off ventilation alone may not be enough.
investigations.modeling_value: Burning rate vs material properties (heat of gasification) and atmosphere; bridges gas-burner tests to solid materials.
investigations.habitat_note: The most directly relevant flight data for Moon base and rover atmospheres: it literally tested 34% O2 at 8.2 psia.
limitations: Pressure per test not in table

investigations.name: ACME CLD Flame
investigations.summary: Weak, highly diluted methane and ethylene coflow flames to characterize lift-off, extinction and sooting at long residence times.
investigations.takeaway: Near-limit flame data that tests whether computer models predict weak flames correctly.
investigations.modeling_value: Extreme-dilution diffusion flames for CFD validation.
investigations.habitat_note: Indirect: model validation rather than habitat conditions.

investigations.name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
investigations.full_name: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
investigations.summary: Applied electric fields to coflow methane flames; the field pushes on ions in the flame, mimicking a weak buoyancy-like force.
investigations.takeaway: The only PSI dataset that mimics partial gravity: a stand-in until lunar-gravity combustion data (LUCI, FM2) arrive.
investigations.modeling_value: Flame response to a controllable body-force analog.
investigations.habitat_note: Use with microgravity and 1-g data to bound Moon (1/6 g) and Mars (3/8 g) behaviour.
investigations.earth_application: Electric-field flame control to reduce soot and emissions.

investigations.name: ACME s-Flame
investigations.full_name: ACME Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
investigations.summary: Transient spherical diffusion flames of H2/CH4 and C2H4 mixtures to measure flame structure and extinction for model comparison.
investigations.takeaway: Tests transport and chemistry models used in fire simulation codes.
investigations.modeling_value: Transient flame structure and extinction limits.
investigations.habitat_note: Some tests at elevated O2.

investigations.name: SPICE
investigations.summary: Measured the 'smoke point', the fuel flow at which a jet flame starts releasing soot, for ethylene, propane and propylene mixtures under co-flowing air.
held_constant: MSG fan-driven flow duct (shared with BASS and SLICE)
measurements: Color video of flame length and soot emission
investigations.takeaway: Microgravity flames emit soot (smoke) at very different conditions than on Earth, which matters for designing smoke detectors and predicting radiative heat.
investigations.modeling_value: 469 test points: smoke point vs flow, a key input for soot models.
investigations.habitat_note: Cabin air only; informs smoke production for detection.

investigations.name: SLICE
investigations.full_name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.summary: Studied when jet flames lift off and blow out in co-flowing air, for methane, ethane and ethylene with nitrogen dilution.
investigations.takeaway: Flame stability limits in microgravity inform how ventilation flow can stabilise or blow out a fire.
investigations.modeling_value: Liftoff and blowout limits.
investigations.habitat_note: Cabin air only.
limitations: Table lists only date and fuel

investigations.name: SAME
investigations.summary: Heated (not burned) common spacecraft materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone, lampwick, DBP) to make smoke and measured the particle sizes in microgravity.
investigations.takeaway: Microgravity smoke particles are larger than expected, so the ISS photoelectric detector design was revisited; this is the basis for next-generation spacecraft smoke detectors.
investigations.modeling_value: Smoke particle size vs material and aging, for detector design.
investigations.habitat_note: Applies to any closed habitat; detection is the first line of defence.
limitations: Some sample grids contaminated (fixed in SAME-R)

investigations.name: SAME-R
investigations.summary: Reflight of SAME with improved particle sampling: 109 smoke tests across materials, flow speeds and aging times.
investigations.takeaway: Quantifies how smoke particle size grows with aging time and flow, so detectors can be tuned for spacecraft smoke.
investigations.modeling_value: Detector response vs smoke properties.
investigations.habitat_note: Applies to any closed habitat.

investigations.name: DAFT / DAFT-2
investigations.full_name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.summary: Checked that the P-Trak particle counter used in SAME works in microgravity by measuring test dust and ISS cabin air.
investigations.takeaway: Validated the smoke-measuring instrument itself, which underpins trust in SAME results; also relevant to lunar dust monitoring.
investigations.modeling_value: Instrument validation.
investigations.habitat_note: Lunar dust could trigger false smoke alarms, so detector selectivity matters on the Moon.

investigations.name: ASE
investigations.summary: Collected airborne particles in ISS cabin air and returned them to Earth for analysis.
investigations.takeaway: Background cabin aerosol defines the 'normal' that smoke detectors must distinguish from fire smoke.
investigations.modeling_value: Background aerosol levels.
investigations.habitat_note: Nuisance-alarm baseline for habitats.

ground_studies.summary: Derived temperature and soot volume fraction fields from SPICE flame images.
New flamelet-manifold CFD model for concurrent flame spread over solids, validated with BASS-II-type data.
Simulated how gravity changes smoke particle growth, using SAME data.
3-D OpenFOAM model of droplet cool flames under heating and drift, validated with FLEX.
Cool-flame flammability-limit diagram from counterflow experiments and FLEX data.
